comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Pipe the response through jq to bind query variables**

In the new `review-timeout-watchdog.yml`, every timed-out PR reaches this command, but `--arg` is a jq option rather than a `gh pr view` option. Checked against `gh pr view --help`, which exposes `--jq expression` but no `--arg` flag; the exact command exits with `unknown flag: --arg`. Because the script uses `set -e`, the watchdog aborts on the first eligible PR and sends no timeout alert. Emit raw JSON from `gh pr view` and pipe it to `jq --arg ...` instead.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Record the timeout label only after Slack succeeds**

When Slack has a transient failure, lines 105–106 have already attached `review-timeout:<sha>`, while the `curl` failure is converted to success by `|| echo`. On every later scan this early return sees that same label and permanently suppresses the promised retry, so the human-review alert can be lost without the workflow failing. Attach the deduplication label only after a successful notification, or remove it when delivery fails.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude processing placeholders from completed reviews**

If the trusted bot posts `Currently processing new changes` and then hangs, `claude-review-response.yml` lines 100–102 deliberately skips that event as a placeholder, but this predicate counts the same comment as a delivered review based only on author and timestamp. The watchdog will therefore remove or never create the timeout marker and will never notify anyone that no actual review completed. Inspect the review/comment body here and exclude the same placeholder state before incrementing `REVIEWED`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
